gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured speed or power figure for any NAS. Macworld measured the 2.5GbE UGREEN DH4300 Plus at 206–228 MBps reads, compared with 99–103 MBps for the same unit on gigabit. Single-1GbE boxes measured only about 100–112 MB/s: the BeeStation Plus about 100 MB/s over SMB (Lon.TV) and the DH2300 112 MB/s in iperf3 (ocinside.de). NAS Compares measured the DH2300 at 9.5 W idle with two 4 TB drives; Macworld measured the four-bay DH4300 Plus at 18.8 W idle with drives spinning.
standout_why: ChatGPT's saved chat shows no search results at all, so there were no rival pages to read. Its answer only showed two product cards (Synology DS224+, UGREEN DXP4800 Plus) with one-line descriptions and asked the shopper to pick a capacity and use. It gives no throughput, power or noise figure. Our current page lists port speeds (1GbE vs 2.5GbE) but no measured result showing what those ports deliver, or what each box draws at idle.
decides: Confirms the split on our page. The drives-included 1-bay BeeStation Plus and the 2-bay DH2300 both stop at about 100–112 MB/s (measured). If you buy one of these, you pay for convenience or a mirror, not speed. A shopper who moves large photo or video libraries gets roughly double the read speed from the 2.5GbE DH4300 Plus (206–228 MBps measured by Macworld), but it costs about twice the idle power with four disks spinning (18.8 W vs 9.5 W for the DH2300 with two disks). The DH2300 measured quiet at 31–32 dBA idle. This makes the DH2300 the quiet, low-power two-disk pick.

findings.label: Measured network transfer speed (Macworld)
findings.value: Gigabit: RAID 1 92 MBps write / 99 MBps read; RAID 0 94 / 102; RAID 5 92 / 103. 2.5GbE: RAID 1 136 / 206; RAID 0 150 / 228; RAID 5 140 / 220
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DH series review: A perfect home NAS for Mac users (Macworld, Simon Jary and Thomas Bergbold, Nov 26, 2025)
findings.note: Helios LAN Test, four 4 TB Seagate IronWolf drives. CPU load was 14–21% during the tests. On 2.5GbE, reads come in at about 2× the gigabit figures (206/99 ≈ 2.1× in RAID 1).

findings.label: Measured power draw (Macworld)
findings.value: 18.8 W idle with drives spinning; 6.8 W with all drives idle; 26 W during data transfer
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DH series review: A perfect home NAS for Mac users (Macworld, Nov 26, 2025)
findings.note: Four 4 TB Seagate IronWolf drives, measured with a power meter. UGREEN's own spec is 7 W idle and 22–30 W in normal operation. Macworld gives no dB figure and calls the fan 'pleasantly quiet'.

findings.label: Measured peak throughput, power and temperatures (NAS Compares)
findings.value: About 280 MB/s peak over 2.5GbE; about 4.7 W idle with no drives installed; 30–35 W in active use; drive temperatures 44–45 °C, chassis/CPU 38–42 °C over 24 h
findings.source_title: UGREEN DH4300 PLUS NAS Review (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews)
findings.note: Large sequential data. The page doesn't state protocol or RAID level for the 280 MB/s figure. Temperatures were taken with four IronWolf drives. The page shows only '1 year ago' as its date.

findings.label: Measured power draw (NAS Compares)
findings.value: About 9.5 W idle (fan Low); 12 W during file activity (fan Auto); 13 W during sustained read/write (fan High); 13 W at max load (fan Max)
findings.source_title: UGREEN DH2300 NAS Review – Cloud Subscription Killer (NAS Compares, Rob Andrews, Oct 15, 2025)
findings.note: Two 4 TB Seagate IronWolf HDDs. The page also gives an 8 W SSD-configuration figure, but labels it an estimate, so it is left out here. No hibernation figure is reported.

findings.label: Measured noise (NAS Compares)
findings.value: 31–32 dBA idle; 33–35 dBA light file activity; 38–41 dBA heavy read/write; 44–45 dBA at max fan
findings.source_title: UGREEN DH2300 NAS Review – Cloud Subscription Killer (NAS Compares, Oct 15, 2025)
findings.note: Two 4 TB IronWolf HDDs. The page has no MB/s figure and says only that the single 1GbE port limits transfers.

findings.label: Measured throughput and power (ocinside.de)
findings.value: iperf3 112 MB/s (944 Mbit/s); Blackmagic Disk Speed Test sequential write over 100 MB/s; power 9–11 W idle, 12–13 W copying over network, 15–17 W briefly under all-core stress, about 1 W powered off; about 110 kWh per year
findings.note: Mac Studio M2 Max client on a 10 Gbps switch, so the NAS's 1GbE port is the limit. Drives were in RAID 1 (models not named). Power was read on a Shelly Plug S, which the reviewer calls 'not super accurate'. The annual figure assumes continuous operation. This page shows no review date.

findings.label: Measured SMB transfer and Plex transcoding (Lon.TV)
findings.value: About 100 MB/s over a local SMB share on Gigabit Ethernet; 4K HDR10 Blu-ray MKV transcoded to 1080p 8 Mbps with tone mapping at about 20% of system resources
findings.source_title: Synology's Beestation Plus Makes for a Simple Transcoding Plex Server (Lon Seidman, Jul 30, 2025)
findings.note: Transcoding uses Intel Quick Sync on the Celeron J4125. No power or dB figure; the fan is described only as quiet.

findings.label: Measured backup speeds (Blackvoid)
findings.value: C2 Storage cloud backup about 26 MB/s average (about 11 min); backup to a remote Synology NAS about 36 MB/s average (about 8 min)
findings.source_title: Synology Beestation Plus review (Blackvoid, Luka Manestar, Jul 11, 2025)
findings.note: Same ~17 GB mixed-file-size sample for both tests. No power, noise or temperature figures.

findings.label: Daily energy figure (Dong Knows Tech spec table)
findings.value: About 300 Wh per 24 hours (about 12.5 W average)
findings.source_title: Synology BeeStation Plus review (Dong Knows Tech, Dong Ngo, May 27, 2025)
findings.note: This figure sits in the review's spec table, and the review does not say it was a meter reading, so treat it as indicative. 300 Wh ÷ 24 h = 12.5 W. The review's read/write charts are images with no numbers in the text. The reviewer did not test the original BeeStation's power.
